resolved_by: Congress's 2024 clarifying amendment, 18 U.S.C. § 3663A(a)(4), which expressly provides that a person who has assumed the victim's rights may recover his or her necessary and reasonable lost income
issue: Can an adult family member who assumes the rights of a deceased, minor, incompetent, or incapacitated victim recover his own lost income and attendance costs as restitution under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act?

sides.position: A family member who assumes the victim's rights may not recover his own lost income or costs of attending proceedings, because the deceased or incapacitated victim incurred no such losses.
cases: United States v. Wilcox, 487 F.3d 1163 (8th Cir. 2007)
United States v. Casados, 26 F.4th 845 (10th Cir. 2022)

sides.position: A family member who assumes the victim's rights may recover his own lost income and costs of attending proceedings as restitution.
cases: United States v. Douglas, 525 F.3d 225 (2d Cir. 2008)
United States v. Hayward, 359 F.3d 631 (3d Cir. 2004)
United States v. Pizzichiello, 272 F.3d 1232 (9th Cir. 2001)
United States v. Chambers, No. 24-11301 (11th Cir. 2025)

this_court: The family member may recover lost income; the court adopts the government's reading, which it says Congress's 2024 amendment confirms.
quote: This issue presents a close question of statutory interpretation that has divided our sister circuits.
cite: United States v. Philmon Chambers, No. 24-11301 (11th Cir. 2025)
